section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces the Socioemotional Selectivity Theory (SST), explaining how social goals and relationships evolve across the adult lifespan, with older adults prioritizing emotional satisfaction and close relationships. It discusses how social networks may shrink with age, focusing on peripheral partners while maintaining close ties. The section also explores the U-shaped association between loneliness and age, noting that the relationship between time spent alone and loneliness may differ across young, middle, and older adulthood. No new studies are presented by the authors of this paper; instead, it synthesizes findings from existing literature.
